title: The Monkey and the Wedge
text:
Near a town, carpenters were building a temple. They were sawing a great log lengthwise, and when the saw had gone halfway down, they hammered a wooden wedge into the split to hold it open. Then, at midday, they went off to eat, leaving their tools and the half split log behind.

A troop of monkeys came down from the trees and began to play around the building site, climbing over the timber and poking at everything. One monkey, whose fate was near, was especially curious about the wedge. He climbed onto the log and sat right over the open split, with his legs and body hanging into the gap, and began to tug at the wedge with both hands, wondering what it was for.

He pulled and wiggled until it suddenly came free. The moment it did, the two halves of the log snapped shut on him. He was caught fast in the crack and died there.

When the carpenters came back from their meal, they found the wedge on the ground and the monkey dead in the closed log.
lesson: Before you pull on something you do not understand, find out what it is holding apart. Meddling in matters outside your knowledge can trap you in the consequences.
